newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling gains on dollar, loses on pound.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling gains on dollar, loses on pound.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling gained marginally against the dollar on Monday amid heavy inflows from exporters and low importer demand, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 55.97 against the dollar from 56 on Friday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 88.51 from 87.76 on Friday.

A commercial banker said the pound experienced an upsurge on the back of British Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke's upbeat speech and signs of new-found unity at the ruling Conservative party's conference on last Thursday.

"This renewed hope has increased investor demand in the U.K. and has resulted in an increase for the pound, which in turn has pulled away demand for the dollar, causing the shilling to gain marginally on the dollar," the banker said.

A currency dealer said "The shilling moved to marginally higher versus the dollar following heavy inflows from exporters amid low importer demand," a dealer said. "There were large sellers in the market but little interest on the buying side."
Dealers said overnight money market rates held between 15 and 20 percent levels from 12-18 percent last week.
